summary: Configured node1 as an inter-VLAN router: eth1 (172.20.1.1/24) into node2's VLAN and eth2 (172.20.2.1/24) into node3's VLAN, with IP forwarding enabled on both interfaces. node2 (enp8s0, 172.20.1.10/24) and node3 (enp8s0, 172.20.2.10/24) each got a static route to the other's subnet via node1. Verified node2<->node3 ping traffic routes through node1. Persisted config (SONiC ifupdown drop-in + sysctl.d on node1, nmcli static profiles on node2/node3). Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node2, node3, then node1 (SONiC router last, since it's shared infrastructure for both VLANs), confirming changed boot IDs and full recovery of addressing, forwarding sysctls, and end-to-end cross-VLAN reachability after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (SONiC-VS)/node2/node3 (RHEL10) interfaces, routes, and topology
Ran SONiC pre-config cleanup on node1: neutralized docker0's class-E address, flushed eth1/eth2
Assigned node1 eth1=172.20.1.1/24 (node2's VLAN) and eth2=172.20.2.1/24 (node3's VLAN), verified pairing via ping to each gateway
Enabled net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding on node1 eth1/eth2
Assigned node2 enp8s0=172.20.1.10/24 and node3 enp8s0=172.20.2.10/24, added static cross-subnet routes via node1
Verified end-to-end ping between node2 and node3 across the VLAN boundary through node1
Persisted config: /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-vlan-routing and /etc/sysctl.d/99-antrieb.conf on node1; nmcli static ipv4 profiles with routes on node2/node3
Captured pre-restart boot_id baselines on all three nodes
Restarted node2, node3, then node1 one at a time via reboot, polling each until exec access returned
Confirmed changed boot_id on each node post-restart, and re-verified addressing/forwarding/cross-VLAN ping after each

evidence.requirement: node1 has a routed interface inside each VLAN, forwarding enabled
evidence.summary: eth1=172.20.1.1/24 and eth2=172.20.2.1/24 assigned on node1 with ip_forward and per-interface forwarding sysctls set; confirmed still present after reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 reach each other across the VLAN boundary via node1
evidence.summary: node2 (172.20.1.10) and node3 (172.20.2.10) pinged each other successfully through node1's routed interfaces, both before and after all three node restarts

evidence.requirement: Configuration persists across reboot (nmcli/ifupdown static config, not just runtime ip commands)
evidence.summary: Static NetworkManager profiles on node2/node3 and ifupdown drop-in + sysctl.d on node1 reproduced the same addressing/forwarding/routes after reboot without manual reapplication

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node2 boot identity change and recovery
evidence.summary: node2 boot_id changed from aad96cc9-... to adeb5b73-...; post-reboot ping to 172.20.2.10 succeeded, confirming VLAN routing recovered

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node3 boot identity change and recovery
evidence.summary: node3 boot_id changed from 739c9792-... to 85e17258-...; post-reboot ping to 172.20.1.10 succeeded

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence: node1 (router) boot identity change and recovery
evidence.summary: node1 boot_id changed from e5168e03-... to 2ed8d579-...; post-reboot state showed eth1/eth2 addresses and forwarding sysctls restored, and both peer nodes could ping across the VLAN boundary again
